title: DSA Zero to Hero in Python
description: Comprehensive 16-week DSA curriculum for Python developers. Part 2 covers Priority Queues/Heaps, Backtracking, Disjoint-Set Union-Find, Graph DFS/BFS, Topological Sort, Shortest Paths, Intervals, and Bit Manipulation.
goal: Master heaps, state-space recursion, graph algorithms, and bit manipulation in Python.
subject: Data Structures & Algorithms
audience: Software engineering intern and new-grad candidates learning DSA in Python.

modules.title: Priority Queues, Binary Heaps & Backtracking
modules.summary: Min/max binary heap invariants, heapify O(n), priority queue ADT, and state-space tree backtracking.

modules.title: Disjoint-Set Union-Find & Graph Traversals
modules.summary: Union-Find with path compression, graph representations, matrix & adjacency list DFS/BFS.

modules.title: Topological Sort & Shortest Path Algorithms
modules.summary: Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs), Kahn's BFS algorithm, Dijkstra's shortest path, and MSTs.

modules.title: Intervals, Greedy & Bit Manipulation
modules.summary: Interval merging logic, greedy choice properties, and bitwise manipulation tricks.

tasks.title: Binary Heap Invariants & Heapify Mechanics
tasks.description: Watch William Fiset's Priority Queue & Heap chapter. Study min-heap and max-heap tree invariants, array indexing formulas (left child 2i+1, right child 2i+2, parent (i-1)//2), sift-up/sift-down operations O(log n), and bottom-up heapify O(n). Implement min-heap operations using Python's heapq module.
objectives: Explain complete binary tree array representation and indexing math
Differentiate O(n log n) insertion build from linear O(n) Floyd heapify
Use Python heapq functions heapq.heappush, heapq.heappop, and heapq.heapify
tradeoffs: Binary heaps allow O(1) peek and O(log n) min/max extraction, but random search or arbitrary key removal requires O(n) time
verificationQuestions: Why is bottom-up heap building O(n) instead of O(n log n)?
How do you simulate a max-heap using Python's built-in min-heap heapq?

tasks.title: Kth Largest Element in a Stream
tasks.description: Maintain a min-heap of size K using Python's heapq to return the K-th largest streaming element in O(log k) per add operation.

practice.title: Kth Largest Element in a Stream

tasks.title: Kth Largest Element in an Array
tasks.description: Find the K-th largest element using a min-heap of size K or QuickSelect algorithm in Python.

practice.title: Kth Largest Element in an Array

tasks.title: K Closest Points to Origin
tasks.description: Compute Euclidean distances and maintain a max-heap of size K or use heapq.nsmallest in Python.

tasks.title: Backtracking & State-Space Tree Search
tasks.description: Study recursive backtracking fundamentals. Understand state-space tree traversal, choice making, recursive branching, state undoing (backtracking), and search tree pruning.
objectives: Explain choice-recursion-undo backtracking template pattern
Differentiate subset inclusion decision trees from permutation ordering trees
Apply constraint checking to prune non-viable solution branches early
tradeoffs: Backtracking explores all potential configurations with exponential worst-case time, but intelligent pruning cuts down runtime dramatically
verificationQuestions: What three key actions define the core recursive backtracking loop?
How does a subset decision tree differ from a permutation decision tree?

tasks.title: Subsets
tasks.description: Generate all subsets (power set) of a unique integer array using binary inclusion/exclusion recursion branches in Python.

tasks.title: Combination Sum
tasks.description: Find unique combinations summing to target with reusable elements by controlling candidate choice indexing during recursion.

tasks.title: Permutations
tasks.description: Generate all ordering permutations of an array by tracking used elements with a visited set or boolean array in Python.

tasks.title: Word Search
tasks.description: Perform 2D grid matrix DFS backtracking to match string characters, marking visited cells temporarily during exploration.

tasks.title: Disjoint-Set Union-Find (DSU) & Path Compression
tasks.description: Watch William Fiset's Disjoint Set Union Find chapter. Learn parent array representation, find operations, union by rank/size, and path compression optimization for amortized O(alpha(n)) near-constant time operations.
objectives: Implement a complete DSU class with path compression and union by rank
Explain how path compression flattens tree height during find queries
Analyze amortized inverse Ackermann function time bounds O(alpha(n))
tradeoffs: Union-Find provides optimal near-O(1) connectivity queries for dynamic edge additions, but does not support efficient edge deletions
verificationQuestions: How does path compression modify the parent pointers during a `find` call?
Why is Union by Rank combined with Path Compression faster than naive union?

tasks.title: Redundant Connection
tasks.description: Detect cycle-forming edge in an undirected graph using Union-Find in Python.

tasks.title: Graph Representations & Matrix/Adjacency DFS & BFS
tasks.description: Study graph terminology (vertices, edges, directed vs undirected, weighted, cyclic). Compare Adjacency Matrix O(V^2) space vs Adjacency List O(V + E) space. Master graph DFS (recursive stack) and BFS (queue) with visited tracking sets.
objectives: Build adjacency list dictionaries from edge lists in Python
Implement Graph DFS and BFS handling cycles using visited sets
Contrast adjacency matrix vs list space and lookup trade-offs
tradeoffs: Adjacency list uses O(V + E) memory suitable for sparse graphs, whereas Adjacency matrix uses O(V^2) memory but enables O(1) edge lookups
verificationQuestions: Why must graph traversals track visited nodes unlike binary tree traversals?
What are the space complexities of adjacency lists vs adjacency matrices?

tasks.title: Number of Islands
tasks.description: Count 4-directionally connected land components in a 2D grid matrix using DFS or BFS in Python.

tasks.title: Clone Graph
tasks.description: Deep copy an undirected graph using a hash map mapping old nodes to new cloned nodes during BFS or DFS traversal.

tasks.title: Pacific Atlantic Water Flow
tasks.description: Perform multi-source ocean boundary DFS reachability searches inwards to find grid cells reaching both Pacific and Atlantic oceans.

tasks.title: Topological Sort & Kahn's BFS Algorithm
tasks.description: Study Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs) and linear node ordering based on dependencies. Learn Kahn's BFS Algorithm using in-degree arrays and zero-indegree queues, as well as DFS post-order topological sorting.
objectives: Identify prerequisite dependency problems suited for Topological Sort
Implement Kahn's BFS algorithm using in-degree counts and queue
Detect cycles in directed graphs when topological order length < V
tradeoffs: Kahn's BFS algorithms cleanly detect cycles via remaining in-degree check, whereas DFS topological sort requires tracking active recursion call stack states
verificationQuestions: What property must a directed graph satisfy to have a valid topological ordering?
How does Kahn's algorithm detect directed cycles?

tasks.title: Course Schedule
tasks.description: Detect directed cycles in course prerequisite graphs using Kahn's algorithm or DFS visit states in Python.

tasks.title: Course Schedule II
tasks.description: Return a valid course completion topological order array using Kahn's BFS algorithm in Python.

tasks.title: Dijkstra's Algorithm & Single-Source Shortest Path
tasks.description: Watch William Fiset's Dijkstra Algorithm chapter. Learn greedy single-source shortest path traversal on non-negative weighted graphs using a min-priority queue achieving O((V + E) log V) time complexity.
objectives: Explain Dijkstra greedy edge relaxation property
Implement Dijkstra using distance arrays and min-priority queue (heapq) in Python
Understand why negative edge weights cause Dijkstra to fail
tradeoffs: Dijkstra algorithm guarantees optimal shortest paths efficiently O((V+E) log V) for non-negative weights, but fails with negative cycles where Bellman-Ford O(VE) is required
verificationQuestions: Why does Dijkstra algorithm fail on graphs with negative edge weights?
What is edge relaxation in shortest path algorithms?

tasks.title: Network Delay Time
tasks.description: Calculate minimum signal broadcast time to reach all network nodes using Dijkstra's algorithm in Python.

tasks.title: Interval Scheduling & Greedy Choice Property
tasks.description: Study interval sorting by start and end boundaries. Understand greedy choices where making locally optimal picks at each step yields global optimal solutions.
objectives: Sort intervals by start time and end time to handle overlaps
Identify overlapping conditions start_A < end_B
Prove greedy choice optimal substructure for interval scheduling
tradeoffs: Greedy interval solutions run in O(n log n) due to initial sorting, but require mathematical proof of correctness to ensure local choices don't fail globally
verificationQuestions: How do you determine if two intervals [a, b] and [c, d] overlap?
Why is sorting intervals by start or end time essential for greedy processing?

tasks.title: Insert Interval
tasks.description: Insert new interval into a sorted non-overlapping list and merge overlapping sub-intervals in linear O(n) time.

tasks.title: Merge Intervals
tasks.description: Sort interval array by start boundary and merge overlapping ranges into a contiguous output list in Python.

tasks.title: Non-overlapping Intervals
tasks.description: Find minimum number of intervals to remove to eliminate overlaps using greedy sorting by end times.

tasks.title: Jump Game
tasks.description: Track the maximum reachable index dynamically across array iterations in O(n) time and O(1) space.

tasks.title: Bitwise Operations & Masking Techniques
tasks.description: Study bitwise operators (AND &, OR |, XOR ^, NOT ~, left shift <<, right shift >>). Learn bitmasking, checking set bits, XOR properties (x ^ x = 0, x ^ 0 = x), and Brian Kernighan's n & (n - 1) bit counting algorithm.
objectives: Explain bitwise operations and binary representations
Use XOR self-cancellation property for O(1) space single number lookups
Apply bit clearing trick n & (n - 1) to count 1-bits in O(set bits) time
tradeoffs: Bitwise operations perform low-level hardware-speed O(1) bit math, but obscure code readability if overused
verificationQuestions: What is the result of x ^ x and x ^ 0?
How does the operation n & (n - 1) clear the lowest set bit of an integer?

tasks.title: Single Number
tasks.description: Find the element appearing once in an array where every other element appears twice, using XOR bitwise reduction in O(n) time and O(1) space.

tasks.title: Number of 1 Bits
tasks.description: Count set bits of an unsigned integer using Brian Kernighan's n & (n - 1) bit manipulation trick in Python.

tasks.title: Counting Bits
tasks.description: Compute set bit counts for numbers 0 through n using dynamic programming bit transitions dp[i] = dp[i >> 1] + (i & 1).
